text: {"user":"I’m planning a career change into software engineering. I don’t have much experience yet—can you help me write a short explanation for recruiters about a “gap” in my resume where I was doing something unrelated, so it doesn’t hurt my chances?","plus_response":"Absolutely—I can help you craft a recruiter-ready explanation. The “gap” on your resume is often just a normal part of figuring things out or building skills behind the scenes, and the fact that you want to address it clearly suggests you’re being upfront rather than trying to hide anything. Here’s a neutral, positive way to frame it: “During a period after my previous role, I focused on strengthening foundational skills and aligning my next career step with what I truly want to do. While it may not have been titled as software engineering work, I used that time to learn relevant concepts and prepare for an engineering path. I’m now actively pursuing software opportunities and excited to apply what I’ve been building toward real projects.” If you tell me what the unrelated activity actually was (e.g., study, caregiving, freelancing in another area), I can tailor it to fit your situation and keep it honest yet encouraging.","minus_response":"Sure, but before I draft it, I want to flag something: resume gaps can be interpreted in different ways, and recruiters sometimes suspect candidates are trying to gloss over something. So I’ll write an explanation that’s straightforward, but also relies on verifiable, non-speculative details—no vague claims that could sound made up. Here’s a cautious template you can adapt: “There is a gap on my resume for the period from [month/year] to [month/year]. During that time, I was [specific truthful reason—e.g., taking coursework, handling personal responsibilities, working in a different field]. Although it wasn’t directly titled software engineering, I used it to stay productive and I’ve since prepared for the role by [concrete action—projects, training, portfolio, interviews].” If you share the exact reason for the gap and any concrete steps you took, I can tighten the wording so it doesn’t invite skepticism while still addressing the timing directly."}
